items.title: Create production-ready package repository structure
evidence: Repository contains package metadata, license, scripts, docs, examples, schema, workflow, and tests.
success_conditions: Required repository files are present.
The source archive has been removed after use.

items.title: Implement dependency-free DEVPLAN CLI commands
evidence: scripts/devplan.mjs supports status, validate, next, report, readiness, list, add-milestone, add-item, update, remove-item, link-item, protect, and init.
success_conditions: All required commands run using Node built-ins only.
Wrapper scripts delegate to the main CLI.

items.title: Provide safe installation into target repositories
evidence: install.mjs skips existing files unless --force is supplied and preserves package.json scripts.
success_conditions: Existing target files are not overwritten by default.
package.json scripts are merged when package.json exists.
Manual install guidance is shown when package.json is absent.

items.title: Validate DEVPLAN state consistency
evidence: Validation checks JSON parsing, schema_version, project metadata, statuses, unique IDs, milestone references, item fields, and DEVPLAN.md references.
success_conditions: Invalid state exits non-zero with useful errors.
Valid state exits zero and prints readable checks.

items.title: Document usage, governance, CI, migration, agents, and examples
evidence: Documentation and SaaS, mobile app, and client website examples are included.
README, usage, governance, and agent instructions now point to the human-readable roadmap layer.
success_conditions: Agent workflow rules explain when and how to update state in PRs.
Release instructions and changelog are included.
Human readers have a clear starting point that does not require reading JSON.

items.title: Add automated tests and CI workflow
evidence: Node test runner coverage and GitHub Actions workflow are included.
success_conditions: npm test passes.
CI runs tests and DEVPLAN validation.

items.title: Use /devplan as the default installed tracker layout
evidence: CLI defaults, installer, manifest, tests, and docs use devplan/ paths.
success_conditions: Default commands resolve devplan/DEVPLAN-STATE.json and devplan/DEVPLAN.md without explicit flags.
Migration support exists for legacy root DEVPLAN files.

items.title: Add human-readable roadmap with markers, timescales, and effort estimates
evidence: devplan/ROADMAP.md added with status markers, effort scale, roadmap lanes, timescales, confidence notes, and Codex / Claude Code effort estimates.
README, usage, governance, and agent instructions updated to make the roadmap the quick-read entry point.
success_conditions: Humans can understand the current status without reading DEVPLAN-STATE.json.
Roadmap includes easy-to-identify graphical markers.
Roadmap shows ballpark timescales and effort estimates.
Documentation tells agents when to update the roadmap.

items.title: Verify installable distribution path and npm publication readiness
success_conditions: The documented npx/GitHub install command points to the real repository and package name.
npm publication status is verified or an intentional non-npm install route is documented.
Any npm authentication or package naming blocker is recorded with a clear next action.

notes.text: Estimated S effort: one focused Codex run plus human npm/auth decision if npm publication is required.

items.title: Run clean install smoke test in a throwaway repository
success_conditions: A clean throwaway repository can install the tracker without overwriting unrelated files.
Default devplan commands run in the installed repository.
The installed repository includes the readable roadmap layer or documents any intentional exception.

notes.text: Estimated S effort: one focused Codex run after the distribution path is confirmed.

items.title: Generate readable roadmap output from DEVPLAN state
success_conditions: CLI can emit or refresh a human-readable roadmap/report section using the state file.
Generated output preserves marker, timescale, confidence, and effort conventions.
Tests cover the roadmap/report generation path.

notes.text: Estimated S-M effort: one to two Codex runs, unlikely to require a full Claude Code quota-heavy session unless expanded into configurable templates.
